title: IEEE 754 floating-point (binary32/binary64)
summary: IEEE 754 is the standard for floating-point arithmetic. Binary32 (float): 1 sign bit, 8 exponent bits (bias 127), 23 mantissa bits (24 with implicit leading 1). Binary64 (double): 1 sign, 11 exponent (bias 1023), 52 mantissa (53 with implicit). Special values: 0 (exp=0, mant=0), subnormal (exp=0, mant!=0), infinity (exp=all 1s, mant=0), NaN (exp=all 1s, mant!=0).

structure.meaning: Biased exponent. Bias = 127. Actual exponent = stored - 127. Range: -126 to +127 (0 and 255 reserved).
Biased exponent. Bias = 1023. Actual exponent = stored - 1023. Range: -1022 to +1023.
Fractional part. Implicit leading 1 for normal numbers (24-bit precision). Subnormals have no implicit 1.
Fractional part. Implicit leading 1 for normal numbers (53-bit precision).
Exponent=all 1s, mantissa!=0. Quiet NaN (MSB of mantissa=1) vs Signaling NaN (MSB=0).

notes: IEEE 754 is implemented by virtually all modern hardware (x87, SSE, AVX, ARM NEON).
Rounding modes: round-to-nearest (default), round-toward-zero, round-toward-+inf, round-toward--inf.
Fused multiply-add (FMA) computes (a*b)+c with a single rounding.
NaN propagation: any operation with NaN returns NaN (except comparisons).
Subnormals (denormals) enable gradual underflow but are slow on some hardware.
